title: Launch convoys and KPI safety net
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for running grouped release waves ("convoys") with an embedded KPI safety net. The idea: treat related feature pushes as a convoy of multiple small waves where each wave unlocks additional traffic and capability. The document defines signals, thresholds, owner rotations, and emergency fallback actions to reduce blast radius while keeping time-to-value high.

Audience:
- Product Ops leads running launches
- Eng leads for hosted & dedicated deployment rollouts
- Oncall and SREs responsible for post-launch stability

High-level concept:
- Convoy = ordered set of release waves (wave-0..wave-N). Each wave has a traffic cap, a short monitoring window, and a KPI acceptance gate.
- Safety net = a small set of metrics and mapped actions that must be observed before we expand traffic to the next wave.

Quick convoys checklist (preflight):
- Wave plan doc published and linked (owner + ETA)
- Canary image and model pinned (model version hash)
- Smoke tests run against model variants (quantized vs baseline)
- Rollback play defined and validated in staging
- Observability dashboards and alert runbooks present
- Stakeholder broadcast channel (Slack #launch-convoy) ready

Signal catalog (primary safety-net signals):
- Latency P95 (API): threshold = 350ms; action if > 350ms for 3 consecutive minutes -> stop and scale down batch sizes / fall back to lightweight model variant
- Error rate (5xx + model inference errors): threshold = 0.5% over 5m; action -> immediate hold, page SRE
- Throughput degradation (requests/sec): threshold = sustained drop > 30% vs baseline -> hold, investigate routing/backpressure
- Token cost per 1k requests: threshold = +25% vs forecast -> run cost throttle policy or reduce model size
- Model quality regressions (eval set): threshold = drop in pass-rate >= 6% on critical prompt set -> rollback to previous model and open regression ticket

Secondary signals (contextual):
- Queue depth at inference gateway (> 500 pending requests)
- Memory pressure on GPUs (> 85%)
- Autoscale thrash (rapid up/down within 2m)
- Customer-facing errors (support tickets mentioning "incorrect answers")

Acceptance gate rules (example):
- Wave-1 -> 5% traffic for 10 minutes; proceed if primary signals OK for 10m
- Wave-2 -> 20% traffic for 20 minutes; proceed if OK and no new regressions in eval set
- Wave-3 -> 50% traffic for 30 minutes; proceed to full if OK for 60m total

Owner rotations and oncall alignment:
- Wave owner: product-ops lead responsible for traffic decisions for that wave (example: Aisha Patel)
- SRE oncall: responsible for infra scaling and paging for latency/5xx
- Model owner: research/ops lead who can initiate rollback or model revert
- Communication owner: PM or comms lead to post updates to #launch-convoy and status page
- Suggested rotation cadence: 2hr shift for first 12 hours, then 4hr thereafter for long launches

Escalation ladder (fast path):
1) Wave owner issues "HOLD" in Slack + tag SRE and Model owner
2) If error rate > 1% or latency P95 > 600ms -> declare incident and page oncall
3) Model regression >= 10% -> automatic revert to previous pinned model; optional traffic rollback to 0% for affected endpoints
4) If capacity limits reached across region -> initiate cross-region failover and degrade feature set (turn off non-critical model components)

Automated fallback playbook (machine-executable steps):
- Step A: reduce per-request concurrency by 40% at gateway (config flag)
- Step B: switch routing policy to warm fallback model variant (lower memory/quantized) with 10% traffic
- Step C: enable aggressive prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts from same session
- Step D: scale up dedicated GPU pool if reserved capacity available; otherwise scale down traffic and notify customers

KPI tracker snapshot (recommended columns for quick sheet):
- Timestamp (UTC)
- Wave id
- Traffic %
- Latency p50/p95/p99 (ms)
- Error rate % (5xx + model errors)
- Avg tokens / req
- Cost / 1k requests ($)
- Model version
- Owner on duty

Example KPI goals for a typical convo launch (numeric targets):
- Latency P95 <= 350ms
- Error rate <= 0.25%
- Token cost per 1k requests <= $0.85 (hosted tiers)
- Model regression on eval set <= 2%

Post-launch postmortem triggers (auto-create if any true):
- Any incident resulting in >30 minutes of degraded throughput or >1% sustained 5xx for 15m
- A customer-facing regression that affects >1% of sessions in a 24h window
- Cost deviation >40% vs forecast for the release window

Lightweight rollout templates (copy/paste to wave plan):
- Wave X: owner, start time, traffic %, monitoring window, rollback threshold, quick contacts
  e.g. Wave 1: Aisha Patel, 2025-03-18T09:00Z, 5%, 10m window, error >0.5% -> rollback, contacts: SRE-oncall, Mateo

Notes and open questions (working):
- Do we want an automated "soft throttle" that reduces per-customer rate before halting the whole wave? Pros: less noise; Cons: complexity in per-customer fairness.
- Consider tying cost throttle to a rolling spend budget per-wave rather than absolute token cost.
- Need a preflight synthetic workload runner to validate autoscale policies against a realistic mixture of short/long prompts. Action: eng infra to prototype by 2025-03-01 (owner: Jordan Lee).

Appendix: quick links and playbook snippets
- Minimal alert rule YAML (example) -> POST to SRE alerting pipeline
- Slack snippet for HOLD -> "@here HOLD wave-X due to latency spike. SRE + Model oncall please ack and proceed to fallback playbook"
- Revert command (CLI) -> `redwood rollout revert --service inference-api --model v2025-02-15-commit123`

Revision log:
- 2025-02-11 created initial draft (Aisha)
- 2025-02-27 added automated fallback steps and numeric thresholds (Jordan)
- 2025-03-04 clarified owner rotations and added postmortem triggers (Olivia)

This is a living working doc. Use the signal catalog as the canonical mapping for go/no-go decisions during convoyed launches. Keep entries short and prefer explicit numeric thresholds when possible.
